rationale: The target directly concerns vehicle braking behavior, so that behavior is itself the phenomenon to characterize, not merely a control mechanism affecting another phenomenon. H-3 establishes the operational context and unintended stopping without an obstacle; SG-3 establishes the prevention objective. FR-7 supports normal collision-avoidance braking as the intended counterpart to unintended braking. P stays at this behavioral level without incorporating sensing, computation, communication, failure mitigation, or mechanism timing requirements.
determining_elements: “Vehicle braking behavior” directly corresponds to the behavior addressed by “Prevent unintended braking.”
The straight-ahead urban driving context, 50 km/h speed, good weather, and absence of visible obstacles or vehicles reproduce the operational situation supplied by H-3.
“Unintended braking without an obstacle in front” is directly supported by the hazardous event in H-3.

“Normal braking to avoid obstacles” is supported by FR-7 as intended braking against which unintended braking can be characterized; P does not separately encompass obstacle-detection or collision-avoidance performance.
No observation, control-chain implementation, failure-response, or timing mechanisms are included in P.
